01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 545

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 545
Sūrat al-Taghābun is disputed [as to whether it is Makkan or Madinan], and it has eighteen verses [revealed after al-Taḥrīm]. In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
سورة التغابن مختلف فيها، وهي ثمان عشرة آية [نزلت بعد التحريم] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 64:1–4 · Vol. 4, pp. 545–547

Verses 1 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. 'Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things.' (1) 'He it is who created you; so among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer; and God is Seeing of what you do.' (2) 'He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and shaped you and made good your forms; and to Him is the final return.' (3) 'He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose; and God is Knowing of what lies within the breasts.' (4)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (1) هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (2) خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ (3) يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ (4)
Vol. 4, p. 545
The two adverbial phrases ("His is the dominion and His is the praise") were put first so that their fronting would indicate the restriction of dominion and praise to God, Mighty and Majestic. That is because dominion in truth belongs to Him, for He is the originator and creator of everything, the One by whom it subsists and who has charge over it; and likewise praise, because the roots and branches of all blessings are from Him. As for the dominion of anyone else, it is a delegation and a trust from Him, and praise of him is a recognition that God's blessing has flowed through his hand. 'He it is who created you; so among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer' means: among you is one who brings about disbelief and performs it «2»
قدم الظرفان ليدل بتقديمهما على معنى اختصاص الملك والحمد بالله عز وجل، وذلك لأنّ الملك على الحقيقة له، لأنه مبدئ كل شيء ومبدعه، والقائم به، والمهيمن عليه، وكذلك الحمد، لأنّ أصول النعم وفروعها منه. وأما ملك غيره فتسليط منه واسترعاء، وحمده اعتداد بأن نعمة الله جرت على يده هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ يعنى: فمنكم آت بالكفر وفاعل له «2»
Vol. 4, p. 546
and among you is one who brings about faith «1» and performs it, as in the saying of the Exalted: 'And We placed in the progeny of the two of them prophethood and the Book; among them is one who is guided, but many of them are transgressors.' The proof of this is the saying of the Exalted: 'and God is Seeing of what you do', that is, Knowing of your disbelief and your faith, both of which are of your doing. The meaning is: He is the One who favored you with the root of all blessings, which is creation and bringing into being out of nothing; so it was incumbent upon you to look with sound reflection and for all of you to be grateful servants. Yet you did not do so despite being able to; rather you divided into branches and split into nations, so among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer. Disbelief is mentioned first because it is the more prevalent among them and the more numerous. It was also said: He is the One who created you, so among you is one who disbelieves in creation—these are the dahrīs (materialists)—and among you is one who believes in it.
ومنكم آت بالإيمان «1» وفاعل له، كقوله تعالى وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ، فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ والدليل عليه قوله تعالى وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ أى عالم بكفركم وإيمانكم اللذين هما من عملكم. والمعنى: هو الذي تفضل عليكم بأصل النعم الذي هو الخلق والإيجاد عن العدم، فكان يجب أن تنظروا النظر الصحيح، وتكونوا بأجمعكم عبادا شاكرين، فما فعلتم مع تمكنكم، بل تشعبتم شعبا، وتفرقتم أمما، فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن، وقدم الكفر لأنه الأغلب عليهم والأكثر فيهم. وقيل: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر بالخلق وهم الدهرية، ومنكم مؤمن به.
Question
If you say: Yes, the servants are the doers of disbelief, but it had already been in the knowledge of the Wise One that, if He created them, they would do nothing but disbelief and would choose nothing else; so what moved Him to create them while knowing what would come from them? Is creating the evil act anything other than creating the doer of the evil act? And is it anything but like one who gives a cutting sword to a man known for highway robbery and for killing inviolable souls, and he kills a believer with it? Would the sensible not unanimously blame the giver, rebuke him, and "pound at his fur" «2» just as they blame the killer? Indeed, their directing of reproach at the giver is stronger!
فإن قلت: نعم، إن العباد هم الفاعلون للكفر، ولكن قد سبق في علم الحكيم أنه إذا خلقهم لم يفعلوا إلا الكفر ولم يختاروا غيره، فما دعاه إلى خلقهم مع علمه بما يكون منهم؟ وهل خلق القبيح وخلق فاعل القبيح إلا واحد؟ وهل مثله إلا مثل من وهب سيفا باترا لمن شهر بقطع السبيل وقتل النفس المحرّمة فقتل به مؤمنا؟ أما يطبق العقلاء على ذم الواهب وتعنيفه والدق في فروته «2» كما يذمون القاتل؟ بل إنحاؤهم باللوائم على الواهب أشد؟
Answer
I say: We have come to know that God is Wise, knowing the ugliness of the ugly and knowing that He is free of need of it; so we know that all His acts are good, and creating the doer of the ugly is His act, so it must be good and must have a good aspect, and the concealment of the aspect of goodness from us does not impugn its goodness, just as our ignorance of the wisdom that moved Him to create most of His creatures does not impugn their goodness. 'With truth' means with a sound purpose and consummate wisdom, namely that He made them the abodes of those charged with obligations so that they might act and He might recompense them. 'And He shaped you and made good your forms'—it is also recited "ṣiwarakum" (with kasra)—'that you may give thanks. And to Him is your return'—so your recompense is for gratitude and for neglect of it.
قلت: قد علمنا أنّ الله حكيم عالم بقبح القبيح عالم بغناه عنه، فقد علمنا أن أفعاله كلها حسنة، وخلق فاعل القبيح فعله، فوجب أن يكون حسنا، وأن يكون له وجه حسن، وخفاء وجه الحسن علينا لا يقدح في حسنه، كما لا يقدح في حسن أكثر مخلوقاته جهلنا بداعي الحكمة إلى خلقها بِالْحَقِّ بالغرض الصحيح والحكمة البالغة، وهو أن جعلها مقارّ المكلفين ليعملوا فيجازيهم وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وقرئ: صوركم بالكسر، لتشكروا. وإليه مصيركم فجزاؤكم على الشكر والتفريط فيه.
Question
If you say: How did He make their forms good?
فإن قلت. كيف أحسن صورهم؟
Answer
I say: He made them the best of all animals and the most splendid, as shown by the fact that a human being does not wish his form to be contrary to the forms he sees among all others. And part of the beauty of his form
قلت: جعلهم أحسن الحيوان كله وأبهاه، بدليل أن الإنسان لا يتمنى أن تكون صورته على خلاف ما يرى من سائر الصور. ومن حسن صورته
Vol. 4, p. 547
is that he was created upright, not bent over, as the Mighty and Majestic said: 'in the best of stature.'
أنه خلق منتصبا غير منكب، كما قال عز وجل فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ.
Question
If you say: How many a ugly person, deformed in form, repulsive in build, is dismissed by the eyes?
فإن قلت: فكم من دميم مشوّه الصورة سمج الخلقة تقتحمه العيون؟
Answer
I say: There is no repulsiveness at all, but beauty, like other qualities, comes in levels and ranks; so because some forms fall clearly below the ranks above them, and because they are compared to the one that surpasses them «1», they are not found pleasing; otherwise they fall within the sphere of beauty and do not go beyond its bounds. Do you not see that you may marvel at a form and find it pleasing, and not consider the world to compare with it, and then see one more pleasing and higher in the ranks of beauty than it, so that your gaze shrinks from the first and you find it burdensome to look at it after having been captivated and infatuated by it? The sages said: Two things have no limit: beauty and eloquence. He drew attention by His knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth, then by His knowledge of what the servants conceal and disclose, then by His knowledge of what lies within the breasts, that nothing of universals or particulars is hidden from Him or absent from Him; so He is the One who is rightly to be feared and guarded against, and one must not dare anything contrary to His good pleasure. The repetition of knowledge carries the meaning of repeated warning, and everything He mentioned after His saying 'so among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer' is, as you see, in the sense of a threat against disbelief and a denunciation that the Creator should be disobeyed and His blessing not be thanked. How ignorant is the one who mixes disbelief into creation «2» and makes it part of it, when creation is the greatest blessing from God upon His servants and disbelief is the greatest ingratitude of servants toward their Lord.
قلت: لا سماجة ثم ولكن الحسن كغيره من المعاني على طبقات ومراتب، فلانحطاط بعض الصور عن مراتب ما فوقها انحطاطا بينا وإضافتها إلى الموفى «1» عليها لا تستملح، وإلا فهي داخلة في حيز الحسن غير خارجة عن حدّه. ألا ترى أنك قد تعجب بصورة وتستملحها ولا ترى الدنيا بها، ثم ترى أملح وأعلى في مراتب الحسن منها فينبو عن الأولى طرفك، وتستثقل النظر إليها بعد افتتانك بها وتهالكك عليها. وقالت الحكماء: شيئان لا غاية لهما: الجمال، والبيان. نبه بعلمه ما في السماوات والأرض، ثم بعلمه ما يسره العباد ويعلنونه، ثم بعلمه ذوات الصدور: أنّ شيئا من الكليات والجزئيات غير خاف عليه ولا عازب عنه، فحقه أن يتقى ويحذر ولا يجترأ على شيء مما يخالف رضاه. وتكرير العلم في معنى تكرير الوعيد، وكل ما ذكره بعد قوله تعالى فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ كما ترى في معنى الوعيد على الكفر، وإنكار أن يعصى الخالق ولا تشكر نعمته فما أجهل من يمزج الكفر بالخلق «2» ويجعله من جملته، والخلق: أعظم نعمة من الله على عباده، والكفر: أعظم كفران من العباد لربهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 546
1. (1) . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "Its meaning is: among you is one who brings about disbelief and performs it, and among you is one who brings about faith … etc." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: He has mounted a blind she-camel and blundered like a night-blind she-camel, and has plunged into a rugged path: whoever travels it is destroyed, and whoever remains in it stumbles. He is only being drained toward the pitfalls of the arāk-tree, hovering around the pastures of polytheism; he investigates, but to his own doom; he pretends to be clever when he is only spouting; he pretends to verify when he is only transgressing. Suppose he turned away from the rational proofs and the mutually reinforcing textual proofs that God, the Exalted, is the Creator of everything, and the principle he claims held for him in the observable world. It is his doctrine to measure the unseen by the seen; yet he has been compelled to acknowledge that God is the Creator of the servant who does the ugly act, and that the creation of the servant who does the ugly act is like giving a cutting sword to a wicked man, and that this is ugly in the observable world, but it does not follow that the like of it is ugly in God's creation. Might it not contain a wisdom that God the Exalted has kept to Himself of knowing? What then guards him against the claim that the servant's acts, though the sensible deem them ugly, are created by God, and that in their creation lies a wisdom God has kept to Himself? And is the distinction then anything but pure arbitrariness and the very following of whim? Moreover, short of his being able to follow these rules: that he should be able to strip the thorny qatād, and that the camel should pass through the eye of the needle.
2. . His saying "and pounding at his fur": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, "al-farwa" is the skin of the head. And "al-farwa" is also a piece of dried, gathered plant. End. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «معناه: فمنكم آت بالكفر وفاعل له ومنكم آت بالايمان
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لقه ركب عمياء وخبط خبط عشواء، واقتحم وعرا: السالك فيه هالك، والغابر فيه عاثر، وإنما ينصب إلى مهاوي الأراك، ويحوم حول مراتع الاشراك، ويبحث ولكن على حتفه بظلفه، ويتحذق وما هو إلا يتشدق، ويتحقق وما هو إلا يتفسق، وهب أنه أعرض عن الأدلة العقلية والنصوص النقلية المتظافرة على أن الله تعالى خالق كل شيء، واطرد له في الشاهد ما ادعاه. ومن مذهبه قياس الغائب على الشاهد، قد التجأ إلى الاعتراف بأن الله خالق العبد الفاعل للقبيح، وأن خلق العبد الفاعل للقبيح بمثابة إعطاء السيف الباتر للرجل الفاجر، وأن هذا قبيح شاهدا، ولا يلزم أن يكون مثله قبيحا في خلق الله تعالى، أفلا يجوز أن يكون منطويا على حكمة استأثر الله تعالى بعلمها، فما يؤمنه من دعوى أن أفعال العبد وإن استقبحها العقلاء مخلوقة لله تعالى، وفي خلقها حكمة استأثر الله بعلمها، وهل الفرق إذا إلا عين التحكم، ونفس اتباع الهوى. هذا ودون تمكنه من اتباع هذه القواعد: أن يمكن من القتاد اختراط، ومن الجمل أن يلج في سم الخياط.
2. . قوله «والدق في فروته» في الصحاح «الفروة» : جلدة الرأس. والفروة: قطعة نبات مجتمعة يابسة اه. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 547
1. (1) . His saying "and comparing them to the one that surpasses them" means: to the one that excels them among forms. (ʿ)
2. . His saying "How ignorant is the one who mixes disbelief into creation": he means the Ahl al-Sunna, since they say that He, the Exalted, is the Creator of the servants' acts, even disbelief and other acts of disobedience; and there is no ground for declaring them ignorant, given that they rely on the saying of the Exalted: "while God created you and what you do." (ʿ)
3. . Maḥmūd (al-Zamakhsharī) said: "He stated it absolutely so as to include everything; then he said: If you say, turning away occurred among them … etc." Aḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: The truth is only that He did not create faith in them nor the ability to it, though He was able to create faith in them and the ability to it; al-Zamakhsharī merely twisted it to his own principle. [.....]
1. (1) . قوله «وإضافتها إلى الموفى عليها» يعنى إلى المتفوق عليها من الصور. (ع)
2. . قوله «فما أجهل من يمزج الكفر بالخلق» يريد أهل السنة، حيث يقولون أنه تعالى هو الخالق لأعمال العباد حتى الكفر وغيره من المعاصي، ولا وجه لتجهيلهم مع استنادهم إلى قوله تعالى «والله خلقكم وما تعملون. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «أطلقه ليتناول كل شيء ثم قال فان قلت كان التولي فيهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: إنما الحق أنه لم يخلق لهم إيمانا ولا قدرة عليه، فكان قادرا أن يخلق لهم الايمان والقدرة عليه، وإنما حرفها الزمخشري إلى قاعدته. [.....]
03
Q 64:5–6 · Vol. 4, pp. 547–548

Verses 5 to 6

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.' (5) 'That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall mortals guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away; and God was self-sufficient; and God is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.' (6)
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ فَذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (5) ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَقالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا فَكَفَرُوا وَتَوَلَّوْا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ (6)
Vol. 4, p. 547
'Has there not come to you'—the address is to the disbelievers of Makkah. And 'that' is a reference to the evil consequence mentioned, which they tasted in this world, and to the punishment prepared for them in the Hereafter. 'Because' means that the matter and the report was that 'their messengers used to come to them......' 'Shall mortals guide us?'—they denied that messengers should be human beings, yet did not deny that God should be a stone. 'And God was self-sufficient'—stated absolutely so as to include everything, among which are their faith and obedience.
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ الخطاب لكفار مكة. وذلِكَ إشارة إلى ما ذكر من الوبال الذي ذاقوه في الدنيا وما أعدّلهم من العذاب في الآخرة بِأَنَّهُ بأنّ الشأن والحديث كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ...... أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا أنكروا أن تكون الرسل بشرا، ولم ينكروا أن يكون الله حجرا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ أطلق ليتناول كل شيء، ومن جملته إيمانهم وطاعتهم.
Question
If you say: His saying 'and they turned away and God was self-sufficient' suggests the existence of turning away and of self-sufficiency together «3», whereas God has always been Self-Sufficient.
فإن قلت: قوله وَتَوَلَّوْا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ يوهم وجود التولي والاستغناء معا «3» ، والله تعالى لم يزل غنيا.
Answer
I say: The meaning is: God's self-sufficiency became manifest in that He did not compel them to faith and did not force them to it despite His power to do so.
قلت: معناه: وظهر استغناء الله حيث لم يلجئهم إلى الإيمان ولم يضطرهم إليه مع قدرته على ذلك.
Vol. 4, p. 548

2. . قوله «فما أجهل من يمزج الكفر بالخلق» يريد أهل السنة، حيث يقولون أنه تعالى هو الخالق لأعمال العباد حتى الكفر وغيره من المعاصي، ولا وجه لتجهيلهم مع استنادهم إلى قوله تعالى «والله خلقكم وما تعملون. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «أطلقه ليتناول كل شيء ثم قال فان قلت كان التولي فيهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: إنما الحق أنه لم يخلق لهم إيمانا ولا قدرة عليه، فكان قادرا أن يخلق لهم الايمان والقدرة عليه، وإنما حرفها الزمخشري إلى قاعدته. [.....]
Vol. 4, p. 548
1. (1) . I did not find it as a raised (Prophetic) report in this wording; it was mentioned earlier at the beginning of al-Baqara in the wording "What a wretched mount for a man to falsehood is 'they claim'", and it was mentioned earlier from Shurayḥ: "'They claim' is the kunya of falsehood."
2. . "And indeed the one who has lived, O Umm Mālik, // will die, and I did not suppose you (azʿamuka) to be removed from that." He says: Even every living thing, however long its life, will die, and I did not suppose you, O Umm Mālik, to be removed from that ruling, or from death. Al-maʿzil is a place of seclusion and being alone, i.e.: I did not suppose you to be in seclusion from it, or to be possessed of seclusion or secluded. Or the very content of the statement, by way of exaggeration.
1. (1) . لم أجده مرفوعا بهذا اللفظ وقد تقدم في أوائل البقرة بلفظ «بئس مطية الرجل إلى الكذب زعمواه وقد تقدم عن شريح «زعموا كنية الكذب» .
2. . وإن الذي قد عاش يا أم مالك
…. يموت ولم أزعمك عن ذاك معزلا يقول: وإن كل حي وإن طال عمره يموت، ولم أظنك يا أم مالك معزالا عن ذلك الحكم أو الموت. والمعزل: مكان العزلة والانفراد، أى: لم أظنك في معزل عنه أو ذات معزل أو معتزلة. أو نفس المقول مبالغة.
04
Q 64:7–8 · Vol. 4, p. 548

Verses 7 to 8

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did; and that is easy for God.' (7) 'So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down; and God is Aware of what you do.' (8)
زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ (7) فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنا وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (8)
Vol. 4, p. 548
Zaʿm (claiming) is the assertion of knowledge; from it is the saying of him ﷺ "Zaʿamū (they claim) is the mount of falsehood" «1», and from Shurayḥ: Everything has a kunya (byname), and the kunya of falsehood is "zaʿamū". It takes two objects, as verbs of knowledge do. He said: "…and I did not suppose you (azʿamuka) to be removed from that" «2». And 'anna' with what is within its scope stands in place of the two objects. 'Those who disbelieve' are the people of Makkah. And 'yes' is an affirmation of what follows 'never', namely the resurrection. 'And that is easy for God' means: nothing turns Him away from it. By 'His Messenger and the Light' He meant Muḥammad ﷺ and the Qurʾān.
الزعم: ادعاء العلم: ومنه قوله عليه السلام «زعموا مطية الكذب» «1» وعن شريح: الكل شيء كنية وكنية الكذب «زعموا» ويتعدّى إلى المفعولين تعدّى العلم. قال: … ولم أزعمك عن ذاك معزلا «2» وإن مع ما في حيزه قائم مقامهما. والذين كفروا. أهل مكة. وبَلى إثبات لما بعد لن، وهو البعث وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ أى لا يصرفه عنه صارف. وعنى برسوله والنور: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 548
1. (1) . I did not find it as a raised (Prophetic) report in this wording; it was mentioned earlier at the beginning of al-Baqara in the wording "What a wretched mount for a man to falsehood is 'they claim'", and it was mentioned earlier from Shurayḥ: "'They claim' is the kunya of falsehood."
2. . "And indeed the one who has lived, O Umm Mālik, // will die, and I did not suppose you (azʿamuka) to be removed from that." He says: Even every living thing, however long its life, will die, and I did not suppose you, O Umm Mālik, to be removed from that ruling, or from death. Al-maʿzil is a place of seclusion and being alone, i.e.: I did not suppose you to be in seclusion from it, or to be possessed of seclusion or secluded. Or the very content of the statement, by way of exaggeration.
1. (1) . لم أجده مرفوعا بهذا اللفظ وقد تقدم في أوائل البقرة بلفظ «بئس مطية الرجل إلى الكذب زعمواه وقد تقدم عن شريح «زعموا كنية الكذب» .
2. . وإن الذي قد عاش يا أم مالك
…. يموت ولم أزعمك عن ذاك معزلا يقول: وإن كل حي وإن طال عمره يموت، ولم أظنك يا أم مالك معزالا عن ذلك الحكم أو الموت. والمعزل: مكان العزلة والانفراد، أى: لم أظنك في معزل عنه أو ذات معزل أو معتزلة. أو نفس المقول مبالغة.
05
Q 64:9–10 · Vol. 4, pp. 548–549

Verses 9 to 10

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'On the Day when He gathers you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will expiate from him his evil deeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.' (9) 'And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein; and wretched is the destination.' (10)
يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ (9) وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ خالِدِينَ فِيها وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (10)
Vol. 4, p. 548
It is also recited "najmaʿukum" (We gather you), "nukaffir" and "nudkhilhu", with ya' and with nun. If you say: What governs the adverbial 'on the Day'? I say: His saying 'you will surely be informed', or 'Aware', because of the sense of warning it contains, as though it were said: "God will punish you on the Day He gathers you"; or by an implied "remember". 'For the Day of Gathering' means: for the Day on which the first and the last will be gathered. Taghābun is metaphorical, taken from the mutual cheating of people in trade, which is that some of them cheat others: the blessed descend to the stations of the wretched which they would have occupied had they been wretched, and the wretched descend to the stations of the blessed which they would have occupied had they been blessed. In it is mockery of the wretched, because their descent is not a cheating. And in a ḥadīth of the Messenger of God ﷺ: "There is no servant who enters Paradise but he is shown his seat in the Fire had he done evil, so that his gratitude may increase; and there is no servant who enters the Fire but he is shown his seat in
وقرئ: نجمعكم. ونكفر. وندخله، بالياء والنون. فإن قلت: بم انتصب الظرف؟ قلت بقوله: لتنبؤن، أو بخبير، لما فيه من معنى الوعيد، كأنه قيل: والله معاقبكم يوم يجمعكم. أو بإضمار «اذكر» لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ليوم يجمع فيه الأوّلون والآخرون. التغابن: مستعار من تغابن القوم في التجارة، وهو أن يغبن بعضهم بعضا، لنزول السعداء منازل الأشقياء التي كانوا ينزلونها لو كانوا سعداء، ونزول الأشقياء منازل السعداء التي كانوا ينزلونها لو كانوا أشقياء. وفيه تهكم بالأشقياء، لأنّ نزولهم ليس بغبن. وفي حديث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «ما من عبد يدخل الجنة إلا أرى مقعده من النار لو أساء، ليزداد شكرا. وما من عبد يدخل النار إلا أرى مقعده من
Vol. 4, p. 549
Paradise had he done good, so that his regret may increase" «1». As for the meaning of 'that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain'—although people may cheat one another on days other than that day—it is a magnification of it: that their mutual cheating on that day is the true mutual cheating, not the mutual cheating in worldly affairs however great and grave. 'Righteous' is an adjective of the verbal noun, i.e. a righteous action.
الجنة لو أحسن، ليزداد حسرة» «1» ومعنى ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ- وقد يتغابن الناس في غير ذلك اليوم-: استعظام له وأن تغابنه هو التغابن في الحقيقة، لا التغابن في أمور الدنيا وإن جلت وعظمت صالِحاً صفة للمصدر، أى: عملا صالحا.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 548

2. . "And indeed the one who has lived, O Umm Mālik, // will die, and I did not suppose you (azʿamuka) to be removed from that." 2. . وإن الذي قد عاش يا أم مالك
…. يموت ولم أزعمك عن ذاك معزلا يقول: وإن كل حي وإن طال عمره يموت، ولم أظنك يا أم مالك معزالا عن ذلك الحكم أو الموت. والمعزل: مكان العزلة والانفراد، أى: لم أظنك في معزل عنه أو ذات معزل أو معتزلة. أو نفس المقول مبالغة.
Vol. 4, p. 549
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Bukhārī from the transmission of al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayra; and in the agreed-upon (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the ḥadīth of Anas in the story of the believer: it is said to him: "Look at your seat in the Fire; God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise." The Prophet of God said: "So he sees both of them." And they also (have) from Ibn ʿUmar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening—the ḥadīth."

06
Q 64:11 · Vol. 4, p. 549

Verse 11

The verse as the commentary quotes it
'No disaster strikes except by God's permission; and whoever believes in God, He guides his heart; and God is Knowing of all things.' (11)
ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (11)
Vol. 4, p. 549
'Except by God's permission' means except by His decree and will, as though He permitted the calamity to strike him. 'He guides his heart' means He treats it gently and expands it to increase in obedience and good. It was also said: it is the saying of "to God we belong and to Him we return" at the time of calamity. And from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: He guides his heart so that he knows that what befell him was not going to miss him, and what missed him was not going to befall him. And from Mujāhid: If he is tried, he is patient; if he is given, he is grateful; and if he is wronged, he forgives. It is also recited "yuhdā qalbuhu" in the passive, with "the heart" in the nominative or accusative. The ground for the accusative is that it be like "safiha nafsahu" (he made a fool of himself), i.e. "he is guided in his heart". It is also possible that the meaning is: the disbeliever is astray from his heart, far from it, while the believer has found it and is guided to it, as in His saying 'for whoever has a heart'. It is also recited "nahdi qalbahu" with nun; and "yahidu qalbuhu" in the sense of "yahtadī" (is guided); and "yahda'u qalbuhu": is at ease; and "yahidu" and "yahdā" with lightening. 'And God is Knowing of all things'—He knows which hearts are affected by gentle treatment and which are not, and so He grants it or withholds it.
إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ إلا بتقديره ومشيئته، كأنه أذن للمصيبة أن تصيبه يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ يلطف به ويشرحه للازدياد من الطاعة والخير. وقيل: هو الاسترجاع عند المصيبة. وعن الضحاك: يهد قلبه حتى يعلم أنّ ما أصابه لم يكن ليخطنه. وما أخطأه لم يكن ليصيبه. وعن مجاهد: إن ابتلى صبر، وإن أعطى شكر، وإن ظلم غفر. وقرئ. يهد قلبه، على البناء للمفعول، والقلب: مرفوع أو منصوب. ووجه النصب: أن يكون مثل سفه نفسه، أى: يهد في قلبه. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: أنّ الكافر ضال عن قلبه بعيد منه، والمؤمن واجد له مهتد إليه، كقوله تعالى لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ وقرئ: نهد قلبه، بالنون. ويهد قلبه، بمعنى: يهتد. ويهدأ قلبه: يطمئن. ويهد. ويهدا على التخفيف وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ يعلم ما يؤثر فيه اللطف من القلوب مما لا يؤثر فيه فيمنحه ويمنعه.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 549
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Bukhārī from the transmission of al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayra; and in the agreed-upon (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the ḥadīth of Anas in the story of the believer: it is said to him: "Look at your seat in the Fire; God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise." The Prophet of God said: "So he sees both of them." And they also (have) from Ibn ʿUmar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening—the ḥadīth."
1. (1) . رواه البخاري من رواية الأعرج عن أبى هريرة: وفي المتفق عليه من حديث أنس في قصة المؤمن، فيقال له: انظر إلى مقعدك من النار أبدلك الله به مقعدا من الجنة. قال نبى الله: فيراهما جميعا، ولها عن ابن عمر «إن أحدكم إذا مات عرض عليه مقعده بالغداة والعشى- الحديث» .
07
Q 64:12–13 · Vol. 4, p. 549

Verses 12 to 13

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'And obey God and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery of the message.' (12) 'God—there is no god but Him; and in God let the believers put their trust.' (13)
وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَإِنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ (12) اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (13)
Vol. 4, p. 549
'But if you turn away'—then there is no blame on him if you turn away, because your obedience has not been decreed upon him; what has been decreed upon him is only that he convey and make clear. 'And in God let the believers put their trust' is an urging of the Messenger of God ﷺ to put his trust in Him and to find strength in Him in his affair, until He grants him victory over those who denied him and turned away from him.
فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فلا عليه إذا توليتم، لأنه لم يكتب عليه طاعتكم، إنما كتب عليه أن يبلغ ويبين فحسب وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بعث لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وآله وسلم على التوكل عليه والتقوّى به في أمره، حتى ينصره على من كذبه وتولى عنه.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 549
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Bukhārī from the transmission of al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayra; and in the agreed-upon (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the ḥadīth of Anas in the story of the believer: it is said to him: "Look at your seat in the Fire; God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise." The Prophet of God said: "So he sees both of them." And they also (have) from Ibn ʿUmar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening—the ḥadīth."
1. (1) . رواه البخاري من رواية الأعرج عن أبى هريرة: وفي المتفق عليه من حديث أنس في قصة المؤمن، فيقال له: انظر إلى مقعدك من النار أبدلك الله به مقعدا من الجنة. قال نبى الله: فيراهما جميعا، ولها عن ابن عمر «إن أحدكم إذا مات عرض عليه مقعده بالغداة والعشى- الحديث» .
08
Q 64:14–15 · Vol. 4, pp. 549–550

Verses 14 to 15

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'O you who believe, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them; but if you pardon, overlook and forgive, then indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful.' (14) 'Your wealth and your children are but a trial; and God—with Him is a great reward.' (15)
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ وَأَوْلادِكُمْ عَدُوًّا لَكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا وَتَصْفَحُوا وَتَغْفِرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (14) إِنَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ (15)
Vol. 4, p. 550
Among wives there are wives who show enmity to their husbands, quarrel with them and stir up trouble against them; and among children there are children who show enmity to their fathers, are disobedient to them and make them swallow grief and harm. 'So beware of them'—the pronoun refers to "the enemy", or to the spouses and children together. That is: since you know that these do not lack an enemy, be on your guard against them and do not feel safe from their treachery and evil. 'But if you pardon' them when you discover enmity from them and do not repay them in kind, then God will forgive you your sins and expiate them for you. It was also said: some people wished to emigrate from Makkah, but their wives and children held them back, saying: "You are leaving and abandoning us," so they softened toward them and stayed; then when they later emigrated and saw those who had preceded them had gained deep understanding of the religion, they wanted to punish their wives and children, so pardon was made appealing to them. It was also said: they said to them, "Where are you going, leaving your town, your clan and your wealth?" so they became angry with them and said: "If God gathers us in the abode of emigration, we will not give you any good." Then when they emigrated they withheld good from them, so they were urged to pardon them and to return to them kindness and maintenance of ties. It was also said: ʿAwf b. Mālik al-Ashjaʿī had a family and children, and whenever he wished to go on a military expedition, they would cling to him, weep to him and soften him; so he seems to have intended to harm them, and the verse was revealed. 'A trial' means a tribulation and test, because they cause one to fall into sin and punishment, and there is no tribulation greater than these two. Do you not see His saying 'God—with Him is a great reward'? And in the ḥadīth: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: His dependents have eaten up his good deeds" «1». And from one of the early pious: Dependents are the weevil of acts of obedience. And from the Prophet ﷺ that he was delivering a sermon when al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn came wearing two red shirts, stumbling and getting up; so he came down to them, took them «2», placed them in his lap on the pulpit and said: "God spoke truly: 'Your wealth and your children are but a trial.' I saw these two boys and could not bear to hold back from them," then he went on with his sermon. It was also said: when jihad and emigration are possible for you, let not the inclination toward wealth and children tempt you away from them.
إنّ من الأزواج أزواجا يعادين بعولتهنّ ويخاصمنهم ويجلبن عليهم، ومن الأولاد أولادا يعادون آباءهم ويعقونهم ويجرعونهم الغصص والأذى فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ الضمير للعدوّ أو للأزواج والأولاد جميعا. أى: لما علمتم أن هؤلاء لا يخلون من عدوّ، فكونوا منهم على حذر ولا تأمنوا غوائلهم وشرهم وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا عنهم إذا اطلعتم منهم على عداوة ولم تقابلوهم بمثلها، فإن الله يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويكفر عنكم. وقيل: إنّ ناسا أرادوا الهجرة عن مكة، فثبطهم أزواجهم وأولادهم وقالوا: تنطلقون وتضيعوننا فرقوا لهم ووقفوا، فلما هاجروا بعد ذلك ورأوا الذين سبقوهم قد فقهوا في الدين: أرادوا أن يعاقبوا أزواجهم وأولادهم، فزين لهم العفو. وقيل: قالوا لهم: أين تذهبون وتدعون بلدكم وعشيرتكم وأموالكم، فغضبوا عليهم وقالوا: لئن جمعنا الله في دار الهجرة لم نصبكم بخير، فلما هاجروا منعوهم الخير، فحثوا أن يعفوا عنهم ويردّوا إليهم البر والصلة. وقيل: كان عوف بن مالك الأشجعى ذا أهل وولد، فإذا أراد أن يغزو تعلقوا به وبكوا إليه ورققوه، فكأنه همّ بأذاهم، فنزلت تْنَةٌ بلاء ومحنة، لأنهم يوقعون في الإثم والعقوبة، ولا بلاء أعظم منهما، ألا ترى إلى قوله اللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ وفي الحديث «يؤتى برجل يوم القيامة فيقال: أكل عياله حسناته» «1» وعن بعض السلف: العيال سوس الطاعات. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يخطب، فجاء الحسن والحسين وعليهما قميصان أحمران يعثران ويقومان، فنزل إليهما فأخذهما «2» ووضعهما في حجره على المنبر فقال: «صدق الله نَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ رأيت هذين الصبيين فلم أصبر عنهما» ثم أخذ في خطبته. وقيل: إذا أمكنكم الجهاد والهجرة فلا يفتننكم الميل إلى الأموال والأولاد عنهما.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 549
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Bukhārī from the transmission of al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayra; and in the agreed-upon (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the ḥadīth of Anas in the story of the believer: it is said to him: "Look at your seat in the Fire; God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise." The Prophet of God said: "So he sees both of them." And they also (have) from Ibn ʿUmar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening—the ḥadīth."
1. (1) . رواه البخاري من رواية الأعرج عن أبى هريرة: وفي المتفق عليه من حديث أنس في قصة المؤمن، فيقال له: انظر إلى مقعدك من النار أبدلك الله به مقعدا من الجنة. قال نبى الله: فيراهما جميعا، ولها عن ابن عمر «إن أحدكم إذا مات عرض عليه مقعده بالغداة والعشى- الحديث» .
Vol. 4, p. 550
1. (1) . I did not see it as a raised (Prophetic) report: Abū Nuʿaym extracted it in al-Ḥilya in the biography of Sufyān al-Thawrī, as his own saying. And ʿAlī b. Maʿbad related in al-Ṭāʿa wa-l-Maʿṣiya from Isḥāq b. Abī Yaḥyā from ʿAbd al-Malik from Bukayr who said: "A caller will call out on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those whose dependents ate up their good deeds? Rise, for before you is the resurrection."
2. . Extracted by the authors of the Sunan, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ḥākim, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Ibn Abī Shayba, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Bazzār, from the transmission of Ḥusayn b. Wāqid from Ibn Buraydah from his father. Al-Bazzār said: "We do not know of any route for it except this."
1. (1) . لم أره مرفوعا: وأخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية في ترجمة سفيان الثوري من قوله. وروى على بن معبد في الطاعة والمعصية عن إسحاق بن أبى يحيى عن عبد الملك عن بكير قال «ينادى مناد يوم القيامة: أين الذين أكلت عيالهم حسناتهم قوموا فان قبلكم الانبعاث» .
2. . أخرجه أصحاب السنن وابن جبان والحاكم وأحمد وإسحاق وابن أبى شيبة وأبو يعلى والبزار من روايه حسين بن واقد عن ابن بريدة عن أبيه. قال البزار لا نعلم له طريقا إلا هذا.
09
Q 64:16 · Vol. 4, pp. 550–551

Verse 16

The verse as the commentary quotes it
'So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend—it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul—those are the successful.' (16)
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (16)
Vol. 4, p. 550
'As much as you are able' means your utmost effort and capacity, i.e. exert your capacity in it. 'And listen' to what you are admonished with, 'and obey' in what you are commanded and forbidden, 'and spend' in the ways in which spending has been made obligatory upon you
مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ جهدكم ووسعكم، أى: ابذلوا فيها استطاعتكم وَاسْمَعُوا ما توعظون به وَأَطِيعُوا فيما تأمرون به وتنهون عنه وَأَنْفِقُوا في الوجوه التي وجبت عليكم النفقة فيها
Vol. 4, p. 551
'Better for yourselves' is accusative by an implied verb, the estimate being: "bring about what is better for yourselves, and do what is better and more beneficial for them"; and this is an emphasis of the urging to comply with these commands, and an explanation that these matters are better for yourselves than wealth, children, and what you are devoted to of love of desires and the ornaments of the world.
خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ نصب بمحذوف، تقديره: ائتوا خيرا لأنفسكم، وافعلوا ما هو خير لها وأنفع، وهذا تأكيد للحث على امتثال هذه الأوامر، وبيان لأنّ هذه الأمور خير لأنفسكم من الأموال والأولاد وما أنتم عاكفون عليه من حب الشهوات وزخارف الدنيا.

10
Q 64:17–18 · Vol. 4, p. 551

Verses 17 to 18

The verses as the commentary quotes them
'If you lend God a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you; and God is Most Appreciative, Forbearing.' (17) 'Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Wise.' (18)
إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (17) عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (18)
Vol. 4, p. 551
The mention of a "loan" is a gentleness in the summons. 'He will multiply it for you' means He will record for you ten for each one, or seven hundred, up to whatever increase He wills. It is also recited "yuḍʿifhu". 'Most Appreciative' is figurative, i.e. He does for you what one extremely appreciative does of great reward; and likewise 'Forbearing': He does for you what one who is forbearing toward the wrongdoer does, so He does not hasten punishment upon you despite the multitude of your sins. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Taghābun, sudden death will be lifted from him" «1».
وذكر القرض: تلطف في الاستدعاء يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ يكتب لكم بالواحدة عشرا وأو سبعمائة إلى ما شاء من الزيادة. وقرئ: يضعفه شَكُورٌ مجاز، أى: يفعل بكم ما يفعل المبالغ في الشكر من عظيم الثواب، وكذلك حَلِيمٌ يفعل بكم ما يفعل من يحلم عن المسيء، فلا يعاجلكم بالعقاب مع كثرة ذنوبكم. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «من قرأ سورة التغابن رفع عنه موت الفجأة» «1» .
